About this world religion map

Faiths of the World is a free interactive world map of religion: a 3-D globe and flat map showing the religious composition of 201 countries and territories, based on Pew Research Center's 2020 estimates of religious affiliation, compiled from more than 2,700 censuses and surveys.

The map has three ways of looking at the same data. The majority view colors each country by its largest religious group — Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, religiously unaffiliated, or other religions — with hatching where no single group reaches 50%. The population mix view is a dot-density map in which one dot represents one million people, so religious minorities remain visible inside every country. The per-religion lenses shade every country by a single group's share of its population.

The world's religious landscape in 2020

  • Christianity is the world's largest religion at 28.8% of the global population, and the majority religion in 119 of the 201 countries mapped.
  • Islam is second at 25.6% and the fastest-growing major religion; 53 countries have a Muslim majority.
  • Religiously unaffiliated people — atheists, agnostics, and those with no particular religion — are 24.2% of humanity and the majority in 10 countries, including China, Japan, the Netherlands, and Uruguay.
  • Hinduism accounts for 14.9% of the world, concentrated in the two Hindu-majority countries, India and Nepal.
  • Buddhism is 4.1% of the world, with majorities in Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, and Mongolia.
  • Judaism is about 0.2% of the world's population; Israel is the only country where Jews are the largest group.

Frequently asked questions

What is the largest religion in the world?
Christianity, with about 2.3 billion adherents — 28.8% of the world's population in 2020. Islam is second with roughly 2 billion (25.6%).
Which countries have no religious majority?
Seven countries in this dataset have no group above 50%: Australia, Côte d'Ivoire, France, Mauritius, Singapore, South Korea, and the United Kingdom. Singapore is the most religiously diverse — its largest group is just 31% of the population.
Why does China show as ~90% religiously unaffiliated?
Pew's 2025 revision classifies people by stated affiliation; most people in China practice elements of folk religion without identifying with an organized religion, so they are counted as unaffiliated.
Where do religious minorities live?
Everywhere — that is what the dot-density view shows. India's 79% Hindu majority lives alongside more than 200 million Muslims, one of the largest Muslim populations in the world; sizable Christian minorities exist across the Middle East, and Muslim minorities across Europe and India.
How accurate is this data?
Figures are Pew Research Center estimates for 2020, published in 2025, based on how people describe their own religious identity in censuses and surveys. Countries with fewer than 100,000 people are not covered.

Sources: Pew Research Center, Global Religious Composition 2010–2020 (via Our World in Data); boundaries and place names from Natural Earth. Map by Suraj Maurya.
